awd_titl_txt: Conference: 2025 NSF Campus Cyberinfrastructure PI Workshop
awd_abstract_narration:
The 2025 NSF Campus Cyberinfrastructure PI Workshop is a PI workshop for active NSF Campus Cyberinfrastructure (CC*) awardees and relevant NSF staff.  The workshop builds upon the successes of the previous workshops in providing an opportunity for recipients of all active NSF Campus Cyberinfrastructure awards to meet to exchange project findings, interact with national cyberinfrastructure experts and collaborate across project areas and project regions. It provides opportunities for additional collaborations by again coordinating with the 2025 Quilt Spring Member Meeting.  The Quilt has served as the co-PI and PI in the series of CC* PI Workshops over the last eight years.  

The workshop provides a critical opportunity for both campus cyberinfrastructure and national cyberinfrastructure experts to exchange ideas, develop best practices, and share both new innovations and some lessons learned.  The workshop has the potential to advance knowledge among the participants in the best practices for operating cyberinfrastructure to support university research through planned as well as less formal interactions between participants both within and across CC* award areas.  The workshop presentations and the workshop final report are being disseminated to CC* award participants and the campus and research community in general, enhancing the broader engagement impact of the workshop.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The 2025 NSF Campus Cyberinfrastructure (CC*) Principal Investigator Workshop successfully achieved its primary objective of strengthening the national cyberinfrastructure community by creating a collaborative forum for CC* awardees, regional research and education networks (RENs), national cyberinfrastructure providers, and campus leaders to exchange knowledge, facilitate collaborations, and accelerate the adoption of innovative cyberinfrastructure practices.

Held February 3-5, 2025, the workshop convened 175 participants representing 124 organizations, including 161 CC* principal investigators, co-principal investigators, and project staff, representatives from national cyberinfrastructure programs, and members of The Quilt. Nearly half (47%) of attendees participated in the workshop for the first time, demonstrating the workshop's continued success in engaging new investigators and expanding participation across the cyberinfrastructure community. The workshop also emphasized broadening participation by actively engaging Emerging Research Institutions (ERIs), Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs), Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs), and institutions from 17 EPSCoR jurisdictions.

The workshop provided a unique professional development experience through technical tutorials, peer-to-peer learning, strategic discussions, and networking opportunities. Participants received hands-on training from national cyberinfrastructure resources such as the Open Science Pool and Open Science Data Federation, explored emerging GPU-enabled computing environments, and received proposal development guidance designed to strengthen future CC* submissions, particularly for emerging research institutions. Program breakout sessions addressed implementation strategies across all CC* program areas while complementary sessions focused on grant administration, researcher engagement, workforce development, procurement, and technical design. Collectively, these activities equipped participants with practical knowledge and resources that could be immediately applied to strengthen campus cyberinfrastructure programs and improve institutional capacity.

One of the workshop's most significant outcomes was the strengthening of regional and national collaboration. Through its intentional co-location with The Quilt Winter Member Meeting, the workshop created unique opportunities for CC* project representatives to engage with regional research and education network staff and national cyberinfrastructure organizations. Regional networking sessions, panel discussions, and collaborative planning conversations fostered new partnerships, highlighted successful regional models for networking, computing, and storage infrastructure, and reinforced the critical role of RENs in supporting multi-institutional cyberinfrastructure initiatives. Participants identified these networking opportunities as among the most valuable aspects of the workshop, providing a foundation for future collaborations, shared service development, and coordinated grant activities that extend well beyond the workshop itself.

The workshop also strengthened the national knowledge base supporting the CC* program through continued expansion of publicly available project resources. Participants submitted updated Virtual Business Cards and project quad charts that document project goals, personnel, accomplishments, and technical approaches. These materials were incorporated into The Quilt's growing online repository, providing a lasting resource for investigators, NSF program officers, and the broader cyberinfrastructure community. Together with the workshop presentations, agenda, and archived materials from previous years, this repository supports ongoing dissemination of best practices, facilitates collaboration among projects, and enables institutions to identify expertise and partnership opportunities throughout the year.

The workshop demonstrated measurable success in advancing the goals of the NSF CC* program. Post-workshop evaluations showed that 95% of respondents would recommend the workshop to others, with participants citing the quality of the technical content, practical relevance of the sessions, and value of the networking opportunities. Survey comments indicated that attendees left the workshop with renewed motivation, stronger professional networks, and actionable strategies for expanding cyberinfrastructure capabilities at their home institutions. By connecting CC* project representatives with regional and national resources, promoting equitable access to advanced cyberinfrastructure resources, and fostering workforce development across the research and education community, the 2025 CC* PI Workshop contributed directly to NSF's broader objective of expanding research capacity and accelerating scientific discovery through a more connected and collaborative national cyberinfrastructure ecosystem.
